Per loose `rendering/**/*.rx2` file (NHL 07â€“Legacy) the 24-byte file table is walked; for every texture descriptor (tag `00 02 00 03`,
56 bytes, big-endian Xenos fetch constant in DW7..DW12) the following are measured:

  DW8 upper (bits 12+, the fetch constant's "base address" field):
    A  == 2 x descriptor ordinal                          (the 2026-09-21 handoff 11 s2 rule, restated for comparison)
    B  == file-table index of the data entry Studio pairs (k-th `00 01 00 31` entry for the k-th descriptor)
    C  == file-table index of a data entry whose reserved bytes >= the descriptor's predicted mip-chain bytes ("join by index")
    the entry class found at index DW8 upper (data slot / untagged NHL 07 payload / descriptor / other / out of range)
  DW12 upper (mip address): == tiled base-mip bytes / 4096 (32x32-element tiles; cubes 6x; single-mip 0; tiny <= 8x8 blocks 0 or packed)
  DW7 pitch == ceil(width / 32) (handoff 11 form) and == tile-aligned width / 32 (roundup(w, 128) / 32 for BCn, roundup(w, 32) / 32 for
  uncompressed — the developer's P2-B form); DW13 byte 2 == mip count.
Also censused: the shipped maxima (width, height, pitch, mips, DW8 / DW12 fields, slot bytes, file-table count) and formats per title; the shipped data-slot byte length per (w, h, format, mips, dimension, packed) shape (a chain writer's output length can be
checked against it). Residuals are kept per title (file, descriptor ordinal, fields; first 400 per class) so exceptions are listed, not summarised.
Usage: python r42_rw4xb2_slot_join.py <out.json> [--titles nhl09,legacy] [--max N]
